traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for Story 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG are implemented and verified by tests and documentation:
1) **Core Functionality – recommended & strict presets (REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS)** - Implemented in `src/index.ts` via `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict`, each an array of flat-config objects that set rule severities. - `tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts` uses `FlatESLint` with `[baseConfig, ...configs.recommended]` / `[baseConfig, ...configs.strict]` and confirms traceability rules (e.g., `traceability/require-story-annotation`) are active. These tests are explicitly tagged as supporting REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS.
2) **Quality Standards & Flat Config Support (REQ-FLAT-CONFIG)** - Presets are ESLint v9 flat-config arrays designed to be spread into the consumer config after plugin registration, matching ESLint 9 guidance. - README and `user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md` consistently use flat config patterns (`eslint.config.js` exporting an array, `js.configs.recommended`, `ignores` blocks, explicit `plugins` registration) and explain ESM/CommonJS nuances. - Integration tests with `FlatESLint` confirm that these configs function as valid flat configs.
3) **Integration with existing ESLint setups (REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION)** - Flat-config integration tests show the plugin presets composing cleanly with a base config that registers the plugin and with `@eslint/js` recommended config. - The ESLint 9 Setup Guide provides full configurations for JavaScript, TypeScript, mixed JS/TS, and monorepo/workspace layouts, demonstrating how to layer traceability presets into real-world ESLint setups. - The presets themselves are rule-only and do not assume a particular parser or environment, which minimizes conflict risk.
4) **Customizable story paths and rule options (REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS, REQ-RULE-OPTIONS)** - `traceability/valid-story-reference` exposes `storyDirectories`, `allowAbsolutePaths`, and `requireStoryExtension` with schema validation and default values, enabling customization of where story files live and how strictly they’re named. - `traceability/valid-annotation-format` offers nested and flat options (`story.pattern`, `storyPathPattern`, `req.pattern`, etc.) that allow projects to define their own story and requirement ID shapes. - Tests in `tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts` and `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` demonstrate these options in action (custom directories, alternate extensions, custom regex patterns, and examples). - `require-story-annotation` also has a well-defined option schema (scope, exportPriority, templates, autoFix), and tests in `tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts` verify that the schema exposes expected properties and disallows unknown ones.
5) **Configuration validation & error handling (REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION, Error Handling acceptance criterion)** - `valid-story-reference` uses a JSON-schema-like `meta.schema` with `additionalProperties: false` to ensure invalid or unknown options are rejected early; tests confirm this behavior. - `valid-annotation-format` goes further by: - Validating regex-based options and collecting configuration errors via `getOptionErrors()`. - Reporting each configuration problem with a dedicated `invalidRuleConfiguration` message while still falling back to default patterns. - Continuing to validate comments and even apply safe auto-fixes where appropriate, instead of crashing. - `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` contains multiple scenarios where invalid regex patterns are supplied; in each, the rule reports a configuration error and still performs normal validation and auto-fix using defaults. - Together, these behaviors satisfy REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION and the story’s Error Handling acceptance criterion: invalid options yield clear diagnostics and do not break linting.
6) **Documentation & user experience (User Experience and Documentation acceptance criteria)** - README provides concise examples of how to register the plugin and apply `traceability.configs.recommended` in a flat config. - `user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md` offers in-depth guidance for different project types (JS-only, TS, mixed, monorepo), with configuration snippets, package.json scripts, and troubleshooting sections focused on common ESLint 9 misconfigurations. - `user-docs/examples.md` adds additional, runnable configuration examples for recommended and strict presets. - `user-docs/api-reference.md` documents per-rule options and behaviors, including configuration capabilities relevant to this story.
Given the implemented code, the targeted tests that explicitly reference this story and its requirement IDs, the broader rule configuration tests and error-handling tests, and the comprehensive user documentation and setup guides, Story `docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md` is fully implemented and verified. Therefore, the status is **PASSED**.
